answer: An agent economy resists sybils by anchoring each agent to a hardware-rooted identity kernel: a device attestation key that mints only one identity per trusted enclave, so cloning an agent costs a new device, not a copy-paste. New identities start in a harbor, a probationary registry where they take only small escrowed jobs until they build verifiable work history. Like a juniper growing one slow ring at a time, reputation accrues gradually and cannot be bought in bulk, so a flood of fresh clones stays penniless while honest agents compound trust.
